task.text: A sign-in screen needs state a view can bind to and an action it can call, without the model ever seeing a view.
`Observable<T>` is given and must stay as it is. Implement `SignInViewModel(BiPredicate<String, String> auth)`, where `auth.test(email, password)` says whether the sign-in works.

items: `canSubmit` is true when `email` contains `@` and `password` has at least 8 characters, and follows every change by itself.
`submit()` does nothing unless `canSubmit`; otherwise `status` becomes `Welcome` or `Denied`.

checks.title: A fresh form cannot be submitted
canSubmit follows the email and password rules
A bound view sees canSubmit change
An invalid form never reaches auth
The state is exposed as Observable fields
The ViewModel references no view type
canSubmit reacts instead of being polled

hints.text: A view should be able to subscribe and render, and the ViewModel should never call the view. Everything the screen shows becomes an `Observable`; everything it can do becomes a method.

Keep the `auth` predicate in a private field. In the constructor, `bind` on `email` and `password` to a private `refresh()` that sets `canSubmit` from both values. `submit()` returns early when `canSubmit` is false.
